# Independent financial-methods and witness-procedure audit

Review date: November 7, 2026 (Asia/Tokyo). Reviewer: financial_review, a separately assigned AI reviewer. This is a focused model-assisted source review, not an attorney's opinion, professional endorsement or certification that every statement in the manual has been verified.

## Scope and result

Read the current complete text of `docs/03-financial-forensics.md`, `docs/04-jan6-and-readiness.md`, `templates/appendix-b-legislative-purpose.md`, `templates/appendix-c-subpoena-and-wave-one.md`, and `templates/staffing-and-recruitment-plan.md`. Tested the highest-risk financial, privilege, historical-team and witness-treatment propositions against the sources below. No blocking substantive defect was found in this sampled proposition review. Remaining untested claims must not acquire a blanket “vetted” status.

## Findings

### FIN-01 — Preserve the existing third-party presidential-information safeguard

Status: supported in the sampled text; no correction required. Appendix C correctly says bank/accountant custody does not eliminate Mazars review. Appendix B's alternatives, scope, evidence and burden analysis is substantively consistent with the Court's considerations. These are not four magic phrases guaranteeing enforceability; the actual matter record and other applicable law remain necessary. Do not simplify the landing page to “private counterparties cannot claim privilege” or “third-party records bypass the President.”

Primary authority: *Trump v. Mazars USA, LLP*, 591 U.S. 848 (2020), official slip opinion pp. 17–20, particularly the third-party discussion and nonexhaustive considerations: https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/19pdf/19-715_febh.pdf .

### FIN-02 — Claim/inference and immunity distinctions are appropriately retained

Status: supported in the sampled text; no correction required. The financial chapter separates temporal correlation, ownership attribution, source allegations, inference and offense elements. It also distinguishes privilege from immunity and warns that private payment characterization does not remove restrictions on using official acts as evidence. Keep those qualifications when extracting short topic cards.

Primary authority: *Trump v. United States*, 603 U.S. 593 (2024), official opinion, especially pp. 6–15, 17–19 and 30–32: https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/23pdf/23-939_e2pg.pdf . This review does not resolve the admissibility of any particular transaction or the application of immunity in a particular state case.

### FIN-03 — January 6 color assignments have a genuine firsthand basis

Status: supported, with the chapter's attribution retained. The official final report confirms Buckley, Heaphy and Riggleman's listed roles. Heaphy's January 19, 2023 interview describes Green funding, Gold election-related conduct, Blue police/military preparation, Red participants/coordination and Purple domestic violent extremism. It also explains DOJ-transcript sequencing concerns. The chapter correctly labels the team account as recollection, avoids asserting an immutable formal organization chart, and does not claim its three upgrades are proven historical root causes.

Sources: official committee staff listing, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GPO-J6-REPORT/html-submitted/index.html ; firsthand interview transcript (team discussion, transcript-sharing discussion), https://cafe.com/stay-tuned/inside-the-january-6-investigation-with-tim-heaphy/ . Interview recollections are not a substitute for adopted House authority.

### FIN-04 — Witness safety and process limits are already material controls

Status: no coercive “flipping” instruction found in this scope. The deposition chapter expressly prohibits threats of state charges, employment consequences or public embarrassment to obtain answers, distinguishes voluntary interviews from compulsory depositions, preserves counsel/privilege procedure, and requires reasonable breaks/accommodations. Appendix C requires real issuance, signed scope, service and production arrangements and does not pretend the January 6 target supplies authority.

The official 119th staff deposition regulations support equal majority/minority questioning, 60-minute rounds, notice/exigency procedures and transcript handling: https://rules.house.gov/sites/evo-subsites/rules.house.gov/files/documents/119th-staff-deposition-authority-regulations-final.pdf . The 120th procedures must be rechecked after adoption.

### FIN-05 — The two volatile financial-regulatory updates checked are real sources

Status: supported as of retrieved material. The August 14, 2026 BOI final rule supports the chapter's warning against assuming a complete domestic beneficial-owner database. The OCC's October 21, 2026 bulletin states January 18, 2027 for its rule and the Act. Preserve the distinction between a proposal, a final rule, an effective date and applicable existing obligations. Recheck before a 2027 operational request.

Primary sources: 91 Fed. Reg. 52508, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-08-14/html/2026-16576.htm ; OCC Bulletin 2026-50, https://www.occ.treas.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-50.html . This is not a complete stablecoin-regulatory survey.

### FIN-06 — Hiring plan is a proposed complement, not employment authority

Status: supported boundary. Independently summed planning seats total 24. The plan does not promise jobs, salary, clearance within 60 days or inherited SAR access. Its employer-specific screening language matches the House employment page's distinction between individual employers and the placement service.

Primary source: https://www.house.gov/employment/positions-with-members-and-committees . The cited committee handbook returned 403 during this run; its current detailed consultant rules were not independently revalidated. Preserve that as an unverified subclaim rather than retrying through guessed routes or treating the source as absent.

## Exact additive wording recommended

Add this short audit label near the document library and in the audit register:

“Independent AI reviewers checked selected high-risk propositions against cited sources. This is not exhaustive legal vetting or institutional approval. Each review records its files, propositions, findings, sources and unresolved questions. Qualified counsel must approve any official process or restricted-data use.”

On any shortened financial topic card, retain this sentence:

“A pattern is a question to test. Timing, shared vendors, wallet proximity or a name in a document do not establish an offense.”

On a third-party-records explainer, retain:

“Private custody does not remove Mazars, privilege, statutory confidentiality or other applicable objections.”

These additions close a presentation risk, rather than fixing a false legal assertion in the sampled documents.

## Verification limits and follow-up

No complete check of every cited state statute, filing, expert method, legal citation, historical assertion or operational endpoint was performed. No alleged individual's conduct was investigated. No confidential record was obtained, subpoena issued, witness contacted, candidate screened or prosecutor directed. Model independence means separately assigned review, not three distinct providers or professionally independent counsel. Future claim-level review should bind the reviewed source bytes/version and invalidate approval when the material changes. A working URL proves availability, not support for a claim. Before official use, counsel must test the actual facts, controlling law, authorizations, rights, access and release conditions.
